english: Let $C$ be the curve $y^{2}+y=x^{3}-x$ in the $xy$-plane, and let $O$ be the origin. The tangent to $C$ at $O$ meets $C$ again at the point $Q$. The tangent to $C$ at $Q$ meets $C$ again at the point $R(\alpha,\beta)$. Then the value of $\alpha\beta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $xy$-तल में $C$ वक्र $y^{2}+y=x^{3}-x$ है तथा $O$ मूलबिन्दु है। $O$ पर $C$ की स्पर्श रेखा $C$ को पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। $Q$ पर $C$ की स्पर्श रेखा $C$ को पुनः बिन्दु $R(\alpha,\beta)$ पर मिलती है। तब $\alpha\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: At $O(0,0)$: slope $-1$, tangent $y=-x$. Substituting: $x^{2}-x=x^{3}-x\Rightarrow x^{2}(x-1)=0$; the double root $x=0$ is the tangency, so $Q=(1,-1)$
solution_full: Differentiate $y^{2}+y=x^{3}-x$ implicitly with respect to $x$: $2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^{2}-1$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3x^{2}-1}{2y+1}$ wherever $2y+1\neq0$.
At $O(0,0)$ (which lies on $C$): $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-1}{1}=-1$. The tangent at $O$ is $y=-x$.

Points common to $y=-x$ and $C$: $x^{2}-x=x^{3}-x$, i.e. $x^{3}-x^{2}=0$, i.e. $x^{2}(x-1)=0$. The double root $x=0$ corresponds to the point of contact $O$; the other root gives $Q=(1,-1)$. (Check: $1-1=0=1-1$.)
originality_note: New: a two-step iteration of the tangent-and-meet-again map on a cubic curve, where implicit differentiation gives each slope and the known double root factors each cubic (way 1, iteration). Closest known: the tangent-chord construction on elliptic curves (this curve appears in number-theory notes, where the first step at (0,0) is a group-law example) and JEE problems 'tangent at P to y = x^3 meets the curve again'. Different because: the question is framed as two successive tangents, needs implicit differentiation at both points and the factorisation with the repeated root each time; no group-law reflection is used.

concept_use.Differentiation of Implicit functions: dy/dx = (3x^2 - 1)/(2y + 1) is obtained by differentiating y^2 + y = x^3 - x implicitly, at O and at Q.
concept_use.Equation of a tangent to a curve: The tangent lines y = -x at O and y = 1 - 2x at Q are written and intersected with C to get Q and R.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy/mpmath and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that O lies on C, that 2y + 1 is non-zero at O and Q (so the tangents are non-vertical), that each tangent meets C at exactly one other point (double root at the contact point), and that R = (2,-3) lies on C. The answer -6 is a negative integer as planned. Changed: the first design used y^2 = x^3 - x + 1, but a published worksheet runs the same first step on that curve, so the curve was changed.
key_step: Using the double root at the contact point to factor each cubic, twice, with implicit slopes.
justification: Two linked stages (implicit slope, tangent, meet-again by factoring with a known double root), repeated; no options and a sign-sensitive answer. Harder than the single-step normal anchor 2023-P1-Q7 (L2), level with average Advanced chains such as 2026-P1-Q1 (L3).
blueprint_concepts: Equation of a tangent to a curve
